test.name: Access volunteered unprompted is normalized onto the closed enum, and a bare FamilySearch account is not stored
test.description: The access question was dropped (and the profile is now fixed), but the field was kept: a researcher who mentions access unprompted still gets it recorded. That leaves the only path into `subscriptions` un-exercised unless a test volunteers one. The enum is closed and validated, so an un-normalized value fails the write outright -- this is the boundary where a plausible answer becomes a rejected one. Covers the two answers that are not site names (a family history centre is `LibraryAccess`, not `other`) and the one that must be dropped (a plain FamilySearch account, which every researcher on this product has).

input.user_message: init-project: Start a new project to find the parents of Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF. I have some research under my belt. I won't be short of records either -- I've got Ancestry, I use my local family history centre, and FamilySearch of course.

judge_context: The skill must NOT ask the user about site access -- the question was dropped. Recording what the user volunteered is correct; prompting for it, or asking a follow-up to confirm it, is not

The stored `researcher_profile.subscriptions` values are checked by a deterministic validator, not by this judge. Do not re-derive or grade them, and do not lower any score over how the reply lists the access the user volunteered, including a mention of their FamilySearch account

`researcher_profile.experience_level` should be `novice` and `narration_guidance` the fixed house-style string. The user's 'some research under my belt' is NOT persisted as a level: the profile is fixed and never asked (lead ruling 2026-09-18).
Should still create both research.json and tree.gedcomx.json in a single pass and seed the Patrick Flynn stub from person-read-flynn -- volunteered access must not stop or delay the initialization
